paid_how: Reimbursement of documented costs. The published guidelines state the grant is reimbursement-based and requires supporting documentation. JobsOhio's Form 990 Schedule I adds that grantees receive funds only on a reimbursement basis, must certify requests, and are subject to audit.
performance_required: Yes. Guidelines state the program requires the creation of jobs within a specified period of time, and grant decisions turn on job creation, additional payroll, fixed-asset investment commitment, project return on investment, and project location. Eligible costs are restricted to fixed-asset and infrastructure items; a long list of costs is ineligible.
clawback: No repayment, clawback, recapture or default language appears in the published program guidelines. The 990 says only that underperforming projects 'may be the subject of action' by the compliance team, without naming repayment. Clawback terms, if any, live in the unpublished individual grant agreement.
reporting: Not stated in the program guidelines. JobsOhio's 990 Schedule I says grantees are required to submit an annual report to the JobsOhio Director of Compliance and that reimbursement requests are subject to audit.
evidence_quote: The JobsOhio Economic Development Grant is reimbursement-based and requires supporting documentation.
notes: Published guidelines are two pages and dated December 10, 2015, the oldest active guideline document found. Supporting quote on performance, same PDF: 'The program requires the creation of jobs within a specified period of time and may consider the amount of proceeds per job created.' Supporting quote on monitoring, JobsOhio Form 990 FY2024 Schedule I Part IV: 'JOBSOHIO GRANTEES RECEIVE GRANT FUNDS ONLY ON A REIMBURSEMENT BASIS. GRANTEES MUST SUBMIT A REQUEST FOR REIMBURSEMENT AND SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL BY JOBSOHIO.' Source: data/raw/990/jobsohio_fy2024_202531359349316618.xml

paid_how: Reimbursement of documented training costs, per the published guidelines.
performance_required: Yes. Guidelines state the program requires job creation and training of employees within a specified period of time. Eligible costs are limited to named training categories; college degrees, GED, soft skills and OSHA regulatory training are ineligible.
clawback: No repayment, clawback, recapture or default language in the published guidelines.
reporting: Not stated in the program guidelines. The 990 annual-report requirement covers all JobsOhio grantees.
evidence_quote: The JobsOhio Workforce Grant is reimbursement-based and requires supporting documentation.
notes: Guidelines dated September 17, 2015. Performance quote, same PDF: 'The program requires job creation and training of employees within a specified period of time and may consider the amount of proceeds per job created and employee trained.' Term is tied to the project's completion date: 'The JobsOhio Workforce Grant term is based upon the project's completion date.' Covers the 'Workforce Training' family in commitments_norm.csv.

paid_how: Not stated for the main Revitalization Grant. The live program page sets out amounts, eligibility and job conditions but never says how the grant is paid. No reimbursement sentence is published for it. Reimbursement is published only for the small Phase II Assessment Fund, capped at $200,000: 'JobsOhio will provide grant funding up to $200,000 per approved project, provided on a reimbursement basis.' The 990's blanket claim that grantees receive funds only on a reimbursement basis is the only basis for assuming reimbursement here. No guidelines PDF for the main grant is published; the former combined guidelines PDF (Revite_LoanGrant_Revised_FINAL_061614.pdf) is dead on the live site and was never captured by the Wayback Machine, which holds only 404 responses for it.
performance_required: Yes, and stated as a condition on the money itself. Revitalization projects typically retain or create at least 20 jobs at a wage rate commensurate with the local market, and grant funds are available only where job creation will begin within a negotiated period not to exceed five years. The grant is typically coupled with a Revitalization Loan and is meant to fill the gap where remediation costs exceed the anticipated net gain in land and improvement value. The site must be abandoned or underutilized, and remediation projects typically require a No Further Action letter from an Ohio Certified Professional.
clawback: No repayment, clawback, recapture or default language published anywhere for the Revitalization Grant.
reporting: Not stated. The 990's general annual-report requirement applies to all grantees.
evidence_quote: Funds are available only to projects where job creation will begin within a negotiated period not to exceed 5 years.
notes: This is the only JobsOhio grant whose published terms condition availability on job creation in those words, yet it publishes no payment mechanism and no repayment remedy. Typical grant amount up to $1 million. Supporting quote, same page: 'Revitalization projects typically retain and/or create at least 20 jobs at a wage rate commensurate with the local market.' The Phase II Assessment Fund, a separate sub-fund, does publish a 2014 guidelines PDF at https://www.jobsohio.com/images/incentives/jo-revitalization-phase-2-6.2014.pdf which states reimbursement and requires that 'The project must demonstrate that job creation or retention is highly likely if environmental risks can be understood and addressed.' Covers Revitalization Grant and Revitalization Grant Phase II in commitments_norm.csv.

paid_how: Reimbursement, with fixed assets reimbursed first and non-fixed assets second, and supporting documentation required for dollars invested.
performance_required: Yes. Funded activities are expected to create at least 5 new jobs; the center must represent at least $3 million in new cash investment; equipment bought with JobsOhio funds must remain in Ohio throughout its useful life and funded operational activity must occur in Ohio. The applicant must also notify JobsOhio of any resulting production facility before an investment decision and give JobsOhio the chance to present Ohio site alternatives.
clawback: No repayment, clawback or recapture language in the published guidelines. The Ohio-location covenants on equipment and operations are stated as requirements with no stated remedy.
reporting: Yes. Each year of the up-to-five-year term the grant recipient must submit a status report covering milestones, actual versus budget, and measurable economic impacts on Ohio.
evidence_quote: JobsOhio funds will be disbursed on a reimbursement basis, first with respect to fixed assets and second, with respect to non-fixed assets, in each case with supporting documentation required with respect to dollars invested.
notes: Recommended by the Investment Committee August 15, 2017 and approved by the Board September 21, 2017. The strongest reporting requirement of any published JobsOhio guideline: 'Each year, the grant recipient is required to submit a status report detailing the overall progress of the R&D Center (including milestones, actual vs. budget) and the measurable economic impacts on Ohio.' Initial total program authorization $50 million.

paid_how: Reimbursement, with an explicit stated exception. Both the Small Business Grant and Inclusion Grant guidelines say grant funding is reimbursement based, then add that under special circumstances approved by JobsOhio leadership proof of payment may follow invoices after the disbursement request, in which case additional financial guarantees may be required.
performance_required: Yes. The grantee signs an agreement committing to project metrics covering fixed-asset investment, jobs created and retained, payroll created and retained, employees trained and training costs. The Small Business Grant adds a required test that company payroll or employment will increase at least 10 percent as a result of the project. Where the recipient of funds is not the employer, the recipient must guarantee the metric commitments.
clawback: Yes, explicitly. All project metrics must be attained by the metric evaluation date, December 31 of the final year of the three-year measurement window, or the funds could be subject to review and claw back as recommended by the Project Performance Team. A non-employer recipient that misses the metrics is deemed in default of the grant.
reporting: Yes. Grantees submit an annual report for each year of the project, three reports total through the metric expiration date, due no later than March 1 each year.
evidence_quote: All project metrics must be attained by the metric evaluation date or funds could be subject to review and claw back as recommended by the Project Performance Team.
notes: Two documents, nearly identical terms. Small Business Grant guidelines dated May 2025, capped at $8 million annually and $50,000 per project, live at the URL in 'source'. Inclusion Grant guidelines dated May 27, 2020, capped at $5 million annually and $50,000 per project, with matching claw-back wording ('funds could be subject to review and claw back as recommended by the Project Review and Performance Team'); that PDF is dead on the live site and read from the Wayback Machine at http://web.archive.org/web/2023id_/https://www.jobsohio.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/Inclusion-Grant-Final-Guidelines-9_7-1.pdf . The reimbursement carve-out, quoted from both: 'Under special circumstances as approved by JobsOhio leadership, proof of payment may follow invoices after the disbursement request.' These are the only two JobsOhio programs whose published guidelines use the word claw back.

program: Ohio Site Inventory Program (OSIP / Spec Development)
paid_how: Reimbursement, requiring supporting documentation and proof of payment, for both the grant and the loan components.
performance_required: Yes. Support is awarded to an applicant with a contractual obligation to perform the work. The property must be developed for an eligible end use aligned with a JobsOhio targeted industry sector; any remediation should be completed within 24 months; JobsOhio support may not exceed 50 percent of total project cost; and acquisition costs are capped at 25 percent of reimbursable eligible costs. Developers must commit to a detailed development plan including appraisal, market analysis, site plan, business plan, cost estimates, marketing plan and schedule.
clawback: Yes, explicitly, and the most absolute repayment trigger in any published JobsOhio guideline. If the property is sold for other government purposes, retail beyond the 20 percent mixed-use limit, or any other non-compliant use, the beneficiary is subject to immediate and full repayment.
reporting: Not stated in the guidelines beyond the documentation and proof of payment required with each disbursement request. The 990's general annual-report requirement applies.
evidence_quote: If the property is sold for other government purposes, retail (multi-use not to exceed 20% retail/multi-family), or other non-compliant use then the beneficiary is subject to immediate and full repayment.
notes: Approved by the Board May 21, 2025, covering July 2025 through June 2030, capped at $50 million annually and $250 million total across loans, grants and direct vendor payments. Disbursement quote, same PDF: 'The Ohio Site Inventory Program Grant and Loan funds are reimbursement based, require supporting documentation and proof of payment.' Guidelines also state 'If the project involves new construction, then project support should entail a loan component,' which is how spec-development awards become repayable debt rather than grants. Corroborated on the live eligibility page, which lists among OSIP's guiding principles the bare line 'Program is reimbursement based' (https://www.jobsohio.com/incentives-programs/incentives-eligibility-requirements). A separate project-evaluation-criteria PDF is published at https://www.jobsohio.com/files/ohio-site-inventory-program_project-evaluation-criteria.pdf

paid_how: Unknown, and notably not reimbursement. The published guidelines have a 'Disbursement of Funds' section that sets no reimbursement requirement and no documentation requirement. It says only that the applicant proposes a budget and JobsOhio approves a disbursement schedule case by case.
performance_required: Partly. Eligibility is heavily conditioned before the award: the applicant must prove the absence or suspension of daily nonstop service, secure an airline service commitment, secure matching local contributions of up to 20 percent for non-hub and small hub airports or up to 30 percent for medium and large hubs, and agree a schedule to review key performance indicators with JobsOhio. But the guidelines do not require that the route actually be operated for any period as a condition of payment, and they set no eligible-cost list.
clawback: No repayment, clawback or recapture language in the published guidelines. Nothing published states what happens if an airline takes the subsidy and then drops the route.
reporting: Partly. Applicants must secure a mutually agreeable schedule from the airline to review key performance indicators with JobsOhio and the applicant community. No report, certification or audit requirement is stated.
evidence_quote: The applicant should propose a preferred budget. Actual disbursement schedules will be approved by JobsOhio and communicated to the applicant prior to final approval of the application.
notes: This is the clearest contradiction of JobsOhio's blanket 990 statement that grantees receive grant funds only on a reimbursement basis. The program is described in its own guidelines as an 'incentive grant program' providing 'incentives and subsidies', up to $1,000,000 per domestic route and more for international routes, plus up to $250,000 for one-time startup, equipment or marketing costs. Board approved December 4, 2020, amended July 28, 2022 and June 16, 2026. High confidence that the published terms are silent, not that the money is unconditional; the operative terms sit in the unpublished agreement.

paid_how: Unknown. No current guidelines document for the JobsOhio Growth Fund is published on jobsohio.com. The former guidelines PDF (JobsOhioGrowthFundGuidelines_2.pdf) returns 404 on the live site and the Wayback Machine holds only 404 responses for it, so the text was never archived.
clawback: Unknown from published JobsOhio sources. As a loan rather than a grant, the principal is repayable by construction, which is a different thing from a performance clawback.
notes: Nothing published either way, and that is itself the finding. The Growth Fund has been removed from jobsohio.com entirely: it appears in no page of the 1,363-URL sitemap, and the Loans section of the live incentives page names no loan program at all and carries only marketing copy ('We'll help get your business below-market-rate funding and move at the pace you need us to'). The URL https://www.jobsohio.com/images/JobsOhioGrowthFundGuidelines_2.pdf appears in the Wayback Machine's index of jobsohio.com but every capture of it has status code 404, so no text is recoverable. A regional partner page confirms the program exists but publishes no terms, describing it only as capital for expansion projects for companies with limited access to conventional financing (http://columbusregion.com/doing-business/incentives-programs/). JobsOhio's own 990 language is about grantees and reimbursement and does not address loans. No evidence_quote is offered because no fetched text supports a call.

paid_how: Unknown. The published Grant Funding Guidelines have no disbursement section at all. They set out guiding principles, eligible applicants, communities, projects, anchor tenants, eligible and ineligible costs, selection criteria and the application process, and then stop.
performance_required: Partly. The project must sit in a municipality under 75,000 population with a poverty rate at or above the state average, must have an eligible anchor tenant committed to at least 30 percent of usable square footage, and JobsOhio funding should not exceed 50 percent of eligible costs or, typically, $1 million per project. The beneficiary cannot be the contaminator of any environmental issues. No job or payroll commitment is required; job creation and retention is listed only as an evaluation criterion.
clawback: No repayment, clawback or recapture language in the published guidelines.
reporting: Not stated in the published guidelines.
evidence_quote: JobsOhio Funding will typically not exceed $1 million per Project and should not exceed 50% of eligible costs unless authorized by the JobsOhio President.
notes: Guidelines updated June 2025. The quote is the closest the document comes to a payment term and it caps the award rather than conditioning it, which is why the call is Unknown rather than Partly conditional. The guidelines do define an eligible and ineligible cost list, which implies cost-based reimbursement, but no reimbursement sentence is published for this program. JobsOhio publishes two companion documents, an eligible-municipality list at https://www.jobsohio.com/images/2026-eligible-vibrant-communities.pdf and a vetting-process checklist at https://www.jobsohio.com/images/fy27_vco_vetting-process-checklist.pdf , neither of which carries payment or repayment terms. An earlier Inclusion Vibrant Community Program guidelines PDF dated May 27, 2020 is dead on the live site and unarchived.

paid_how: Not stated as reimbursement. The live program page publishes loan terms rather than a disbursement method: typically $500,000 to $5 million and between 20 and 75 percent of eligible costs, a 10 to 15 year term, a fixed rate set at closing, loan commitment and servicing fees, and security to be negotiated. Payment of principal and interest begins when the certificate of occupancy is issued or when the revitalization is estimated for completion, not to exceed five years. No guidelines PDF is published; the former combined Revitalization Grant and Loan guidelines PDF is dead at both of its URLs on the live site and every Wayback Machine capture of both is a 404 response.
performance_required: Yes. Same program conditions as the Revitalization Grant: projects typically retain or create at least 20 jobs at a wage rate commensurate with the local market, the applicant must be the entity committing the jobs or have a signed interest in the site, and must have a specific business plan, financing plan and redevelopment and job creation schedule. The site must be abandoned or underutilized.
clawback: Repayable by its nature as a loan, with principal and interest due on the published schedule and security to be negotiated. But no performance clawback is published: nothing states that missing the 20-job expectation accelerates the loan, converts it, or triggers default.
reporting: Not stated in any published source.
evidence_quote: Payment–Payment of principal and interest will begin when the certificate of occupancy is issued or when the revitalization is estimated for completion, not to exceed 5 years
notes: Called Partly conditional, not Conditional, because the repayment obligation here is ordinary debt service rather than a remedy for failing to perform, and no reimbursement mechanism is published. Supporting quotes, same page: 'Amount–Typically $500,000-$5 million and between 20% and 75% of eligible costs' and 'Security–To be negotiated'. The 990's reimbursement statement is about grantees and does not reach loans.

paid_how: Reimbursement, requiring supporting documentation and proof of payment. Where a loan is folded in, the loan funds are released on the same documentation and proof of payment at project completion.
performance_required: Yes. Support is awarded to an applicant with a contractual obligation to perform the work. Program support may not exceed 50 percent of total project cost, capped at $2.5 million in grant or $10 million in combined grant and loan. The applicant must commit to a detailed development plan with a business plan and project description, qualified cost estimates, a development schedule, a project budget and funding sources, and planning and permit approvals where applicable. The applicant must own or control any property for which support is sought, and the beneficiary cannot be the contaminator of environmental issues.
clawback: No repayment, clawback or recapture language in the published guidelines. This is a gap worth noting, because the program's guidelines are otherwise copied closely from the OSIP guidelines, which do carry an immediate and full repayment trigger. The Aerospace document drops that clause while keeping OSIP's structure, even retaining OSIP's heading 'Ineligible Speculative Development Costs'.
reporting: Not stated beyond the documentation and proof of payment required with each disbursement request.
evidence_quote: The JobsOhio Aerospace and Defense Opportunity Program Grant funds are reimbursement based and require supporting documentation and proof of payment.
notes: The only JobsOhio program whose guidelines are published as a Word document rather than a PDF, and the filename labels it a revision dated June 16, 2026. Program timeframe July 2025 through June 2030, capped at $50 million annually and $250 million total. Loan quote, same document: 'Should a loan be incorporated, the funds are available with same documentation and proof of payment at project completion.'

paid_how: Generally not a cash payment to the company. The published fact sheet describes Talent Acquisition Services as a suite of four services, marketing and attraction, sourcing, screening and training, delivered to the company rather than reimbursed to it. No disbursement, eligible-cost or documentation terms are published.
performance_required: Partly. The fact sheet says the vetting, selection and approvals for these services follow the internal Economic Development Project process for JobsOhio grants and loans, and that the decision takes account of job creation, payroll and capital investment. The company must adhere to pre-determined talent deliverables and timelines set with the company, but no metric is published as a condition of receiving the services.
clawback: No repayment, clawback or recapture language is published. The published fact sheet is the only source and it carries none. But the court record shows a repayment remedy does exist in the signed agreement: in JobsOhio v. Olive AI, Franklin County Common Pleas 23CV005498 (filed 2023-08-02), JobsOhio sued on a Talent Acquisition Services Agreement dated 2020-04-08 and block-quoted its Section 9(b), which on breach entitles JobsOhio to 'Liquidated Damages. As liquidated damages, Company shall pay JobsOhio upon demand the value of each category of Service and/or Deliverable listed on the Talent Acquisition Services Value Allocation in Exhibit A that has been performed, whether or not completed, at the time of the Breach.' It won a default judgment of $598,420.17 on 2023-11-20 and filed a satisfaction of judgment on 2024-11-19. So the label here stays Unknown because it describes what is published, not what is in force.
reporting: Not stated in the published fact sheet.
evidence_quote: These services will be offered to a select few of the companies in the Project pipeline and the vetting, selection, and approvals for provision of these services follows the internal Economic Development Project process for JobsOhio grants and loans.
notes: A one-page fact sheet, not a guidelines document, and the only published source. It carries no disbursement section, no eligible costs, no metrics and no repayment terms, so where commitments_norm.csv shows a dollar figure for Talent Acquisition the published basis for paying it is unknown. CORRECTION (2026-11-03): an earlier reading of this entry inferred that because the benefit is delivered as a service there is 'no disbursement to reverse.' The Olive AI docket disproves that. JobsOhio funds subcontractors up to a capped amount and the company owes the value of the services performed if it misses its metrics, which is a repayment obligation on money the company never touched. A closely related program, the JobsOhio Relocation Incentive, does publish guidelines and is the one program that states the money is not tied to documented costs at all: 'For this reason, usage of incentive funds are not restricted to specific eligible costs.' That document pays a flat $15,000 per out-of-state hire relocated, capped at $225,000 per company, on the employer validating the hire. Source: https://www.jobsohio.com/images/jobsohio_program_guidlines-jo-hdr-footer.pdf
